svg.title: Voyage of HMT Empire Windrush & The Making of Multicultural Britain (1948–59)
svg.desc: KS3 historical GIS transatlantic atlas map showing HMT Empire Windrush's May–June 1948 8,000-mile voyage from Trinidad, Kingston (Jamaica), Tampico (Mexico), Havana, and Bermuda across the Atlantic Ocean to Tilbury Docks (Essex) on 22 June 1948, paired with a zoomed Greater London and Thames Estuary GIS panel highlighting Tilbury Docks, Clapham South Deep Shelter, Brixton, Notting Hill (1958 riots), and Claudia Jones's 1959 Caribbean Carnival.

g.text: KEY — EMPIRE WINDRUSH VOYAGE & MULTICULTURAL LONDON
British Caribbean Colonies (CUKC Equal Citizens under 1948 Act)
Great Britain ('Mother Country' • Post-War Labour Shortage)
Key Windrush London Boroughs (Zoomed Panel Above)
Lambeth (Clapham Shelter & Brixton), Kensington (Notting Hill) & Camden (St Pancras)
Arrival Transfer: Tilbury Docks → Clapham South Deep Shelter

text.tspan: Historic arrival; Clapham South deep shelter
houses new NHS, rail & transport workers

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: RIGHTS & POST-WAR BRITAIN
Voyage of HMT Empire Windrush & Multicultural Britain (1948–1959)
Under the 1948 British Nationality Act, Caribbean citizens sailed aboard HMT Empire Windrush to rebuild Britain’s NHS, railways, and buses.
Despite harsh housing “colour bars” and the 1958 Notting Hill riots, pioneers like Claudia Jones forged vibrant Black British community life.
